sector_model: Subscription software: GAAP P/E, FCF after capitalised software and SBC, net cash, buybacks, management change.
thesis: HubSpot (NYSE: HUBS), CRM software for small and mid-size businesses. Q3 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-11-04) read: balance sheet, income statement, cash flow lines, buyback note. Q3 revenue 947.6M (+17.1%), 9M 2,740.3M (+20.0%); subscription 930.2M; Q3 GAAP NI 83.0M vs 16.5M; 9M NI 158.9M. Close 193.88 (2026-11-20) x 48,836,461 shares (2026-10-30 cover) = 9.47B = 44.4x TTM NI 213.3M (45.9+8.5+158.9). TTM OCF 907.0M; capex 64.5M plus capitalised software 143.3M; FCF after both 699.2M (7.4%), but TTM SBC 503.7M, so FCF after SBC is about 195M (2.1%, own estimate). No debt line on the balance sheet (2025 convertible notes repaid); cash 1,121.3M, short-term investments 175.4M. Buybacks 973.7M in 9M funded by running down investments (short-term investments 821.6M to 175.4M); 1.0B remains authorised. 8-K 5.02 filed 2026-11-12: CEO Yamini Rangan stepped down effective 11-12 and co-founder Brian Halligan returned as CEO. Stock fell from 231.98 (11-16) to 193.88 (-16.4% in 3 sessions) and was bought back at about 224 after quarter end.
counterthesis: A 44x GAAP multiple with a sudden CEO change one week after earnings is a governance and execution flag; reason for the exit is not stated in the 8-K text read. Real owner earnings are far below headline FCF once SBC (about 18% of TTM revenue, own estimate) is counted; share count fell only because buybacks absorb dilution. AI-driven disruption of SMB CRM seats is a recognised risk but not read here. Buybacks at about 224 are now well above the 193.88 price.
invalidation: Downgrade if growth decelerates below the mid teens, the CEO change reflects undisclosed problems, or SBC keeps consuming most of FCF. Upgrade case needs the Q3 release and call, net revenue retention, peers (CRM, ADBE, WDAY, DDOG), and verified quote origins.
